docs.title: Welcome to the Powdered World Engine Documentation!
docs.text:
Just a few things before we get started...

  • Powdered World Engine will sometimes be referred to as PWEngine. Just remember that they mean the same thing!

  • When referring to an individual pixel in the simulation, it can be called a "cell" or an "element".

docs.title: About
docs.text: I thought this was a cool project, wbu? also I made this in high school, so dont expect some professional-grade stuff here XD

This class is made from autogenerating a script from strings so an element enum can be dynamically changed when interacting with the element creation editor tab. It contains the AllElements Enum and a few helper functions.

docs.title: Enum AllElements
docs.text:
An Enum containing every element created in the Element Editor tab. Dynamically changed when the Apply Changes button in the element tab is pressed.

It has some default values:

Value AIR SAND WATER ACID STONE WALL

docs.title: PowderSimulation
docs.text:
Inherits: Node2D < CanvasItem < Node < Object

This node is what you will use to handle individual simulations. It could be called an "orchestrator" class for the simulation, as it does not define the base chunk or cell classes, but simply contains them and tells them what to do. It also contains useful methods for maniplulating the world, such as placing elements or clearing all cells.

NOTE: This node defines _Ready() and _Draw(), so if you are attaching a script to this node and using those functions, make sure to include super() in it so it still calls the parent class functions as well as whatever you put.

docs.title: void FillWorld(AllElements with)
docs.text: Replaces every cell in the current world with the element specified in with.

docs.title: void ClearWorld()
docs.text: Replaces every cell in the current world with AllElements.AIR. Functionally equivalent to calling FillWorld(AllElements.AIR).

docs.title: Vector2I WorldToLocal(Vector2 from_world)
docs.text:
• Vector2 from_world - the world-space coordinates to find the closest element from. world-space is the same as global_position for Nodes.

Returns the given cell world position (Godot's regular global_position for nodes) translated into local simulation position.

docs.title: Vector2 LocalToWorld(Vector2I fromLocal, bool includeParentOffset = true)
docs.text:
• Vector2I fromLocal - the local-space coordinates to translate to world-space.
  • bool includeParentOffset - Whether or not to include the offset of the PowderSimulation parent Node in the calculation.

Returns the given chunk local simulation position translated into world position.

docs.title: bool PlaceElement(Vector2I pos, AllElements element, bool overRide = false)
docs.text:
• Vector2I pos - the local-space coordinates to the cell where the specified element will be placed.
  • AllElements element - the element to replace the specified cell's element with.
  • bool overRide - if false, only places the specified element if the cell's element is AIR.

Replaces the element of the cell at pos with element. If overRide is set to true, overrides the element of the cell at pos regardless of what it already is. If overRide is true, only changes the element if the element of the cell is already AIR.

Returns true if the placement succeeded, otherwise returns false.

Ex. PlaceElement(Vector2I(0, 0), AllElements.SAND, true) will replace the cell at pos (0, 0)'s element with element, regardless of the element it was beforehand because overRide was set to true.

docs.title: void PlaceGroupElements(int brushSize, Vector2I pos, AllElements element, bool overRide = false)
docs.text:
• int brushSize - the amount the square placement pattern expands in all four directions.

Calls PlaceElement repeatedly in a square pattern which starts at pos and expands outward brushSize times.

Ex. brushSize = 0 will place a single element, and brushsize = 1 will place a group of nine elements, starting from pos and extending 1 cell in all four directions.

docs.title: void SetWorldStreamer(WorldStreamer NewStreamer)
docs.text:
• WorldStreamer NewStreamer - The WorldStreamer instance to assign.

Assigns a WorldStreamer object to the simulation. When assigned, using FollowMode will save/load chunks using the WorldStreamer object. Set to null to disable this behavior.

Returns the chunk currently at pos. Throws an error if there is no chunk at pos.

docs.title: void SetFollowMode(bool to)
docs.text:
bool to - The boolean to set FollowEnabled to.

Sets FollowEnabled to to.

docs.title: void SetFollowNode(Node2D what)
docs.text:
Node2D what - The node to set FollowNode to.

Sets the node for the simulation to follow. If FollowEnabled is set to true, the simulation uses the Node2D's position to determine where the constraints are centered.

docs.title: void SetConstraints(Vector2 to)
docs.text:
Vector2 to - What to set the constraints to.

Sets the constraints for the simulation. If FollowEnabled is set to true, the simulation auto loads/unloads chunks to fill the range ± to.

docs.title: Vector2 ChunkLocalToWorld(Vector2I fromLocal, bool includeParentOffset = true)
docs.text:
Vector2I fromLocal - The local chunk position in which to transform. bool includeParentOffset - Whether or not to include the offset of the the parent node in the calculation. For example, if the position of the chunk is (32, 32) and the local position of this node is (10, 10) the final position will be (42, 42).

Returns the given chunk local simulation position translated into world position.

docs.title: Vector2I LocalToChunk(Vector2I localPos)
docs.text:
Vector2I localPos - The local simulation position (position of a cell) to convert to chunk position.

Returns the local simulation position to chunk coordinates. Truncates decimals toward zero. Used for finding a cell's chunk from just the position.

docs.title: Vector2I WorldToChunk(Vector2 worldPos)
docs.text:
Vector2I worldPos - The world position (same as global_position for Node2Ds) converted to local chunk position.

Returns the given global (world) position converted to local chunk position.

docs.title: void QueueSwap(SandInfo.Cell Cell1, SandInfo.Cell Cell2)
docs.text:
SandInfo.Cell Cell1 - The first cell to swap. SandInfo.Cell Cell2 - The second cell to swap.

Adds two cells to list of cells to be swapped at the end of the frame.

docs.title: void CommitSwapQueue()
docs.text: Writes all the buffered swaps onto the simulation.

docs.title: bool AddChunk(Vector2I at)
docs.text:
Vector2I at - The chunk position at which the new chunk will be created.

Adds an empty chunk at the specified coordinates. Returns whether or not the chunk was successfully added.

docs.title: bool RemoveChunk(Vector2I at)
docs.text:
Vector2I at - The chunk position at which the chunk will be removed.

Removes the chunk at the specified coordinates. Returns whether there was a chunk at the specified position or not.

docs.title: void InitGrid()
docs.text: Populates the grid with Chunk and Cell objects set to the correct default state. One of the functions called in this node's _Ready() function.

docs.title: void UpdateChunks(int tick)
docs.text:
int tick - The elapsed frame, mod by two (constrained to 0 and 1). Changes update direction based on the current tick, making the simulation less one-sided.

Updates the cells in all the chunks of the simulation, sending them to the swap buffer. Automatically called in UpdateSimulation().

docs.title: void DecideSleepingChunks()
docs.text: Updates the sleep state of each chunk in the simulation decided by their insomnia count. There are currently no functions that require this to be called as UpdateChunks() does it itself.

docs.title: void RenderChunkUpdates()
docs.text: Loops through each chunk and sends its cell data to its respective ChunkRenderer.

docs.title: void UpdateSimulationSize()
docs.text: Updates the simulation_size variable if chunk grid size has been changed. This is automatically done, so no need to call this.

docs.title: void UpdateSimulation(bool wait = true)
docs.text:
bool wait - Whether or not to check if the correct amount of time has passed specified in SimulationSpeed, and if not, does not call the function.

Updates the simulation while being safe to put in _Process/_PhysicsProcess because if wait is set to true, it will not tick until the right amount of time has passed specified in SimulationSpeed. If wait is set to false, runs one tick of the simulation regardless.

docs.title: SandInfo.Cell GetCell(Vector2I pos)
docs.text:
Vector2I pos - The position to get the cell from.

Returns the cell at the specified pos. Throws an error if a cell does not exist at pos.

docs.title: void SetCell(Vector2I pos, AllElements element)
docs.text:
Vector2I pos - The position to get the cell for editing. AllElements element - The element to change the cell to.

Replaces the element at pos with element.

docs.title: float SimulationSpeed
docs.text: How fast the simulation runs, with 1.0 corresponding with 60 updates/second.

docs.title: bool UseDirtyRects
docs.text: Dirty rects are rectangles calculated at runtime that only contain the cells that were updated in the last frame, lowering the total number of cells needing updates. Recommended for chunk sizes 32 and above.

docs.title: int IndividualChunkSize
docs.text: How many cells squared each cell contains. It is squared because the chunk size is only measured on one axis.

docs.title: Vector2I ChunkGridSize
docs.text: How many chunks to be used in the simulation.

docs.title: int ChunkInsomnia
docs.text: How many update loops with no change in a specific chunk have to occur before sleeping the chunk.

docs.title: bool Centered
docs.text: Whether the simulation appears at the center of this Node's position or offset like Control Nodes are.

docs.title: int PixelScale
docs.text: How big the pixels appear on the screen.

docs.title: bool FollowEnabled
docs.text:
Whether or not to use the Node Follow feature.

Node Follow constrains the simulation to a certain size by unloading/loading chunks dynamically as the FollowNode's position changes. It also works with the filesystem if a WorldStreamer is set with SetWorldStreamer().

docs.title: Node2D FollowNode
docs.text: The Node to follow when FollowEnabled is true.

docs.title: Rect2 FollowAreaConstraint
docs.text: The size to constrain the simulation in when FollowEnabled is true. DO NOT set the Position property of the Rect2, it will get overridden.

docs.title: bool FollowCenterConstraintsOnFollowedNode
docs.text: Whether or not to center the constraints on FollowNode by setting FollowAreaConstraint.Position to -(FollowAreaConstraint.Size / 2.0). Only effective when FollowEnabled is true.

docs.title: bool DebugMode
docs.text: Draws a visual of chunk borders and dirty rects.

docs.title: Color DebugChunkBorderColor
docs.text: What color to display the chunk borders as when DebugMode is true.

docs.title: bool ShowSimBorder
docs.text: Draws a rectangular border around the entire simulation.

docs.title: int SimBorderWidth
docs.text: How wide the line at the simulation border will be.

docs.title: Dictionary<Vector2I, SandInfo.Chunk> Chunks
docs.text: The current chunks in the simulation mapped to their positions.

docs.title: Vector2I SimulationSize
docs.text: The size of all the cells in the simulation, basically the max extents of the simulation if the top-left corner was (0, 0)

docs.title: Vector2I SimulationMaxExtents
docs.text: The bottom-rightmost cell position in the simulation.

docs.title: Vector2I SimulationMinExtents
docs.text: The top-leftmost cell position in the simulation.

docs.title: float UpdateTime
docs.text: The amount of time it took this frame to update the simulation. Used for debug purposes.

docs.title: float DrawTime
docs.text: The amount of time it took this frame to draw the simulation. Used for debug purposes.

docs.title: List<ChunkRendererCS> ActiveChunkRenderers
docs.text: The active ChunkRendererCSs in the simulation. There is one ChunkRenderer per chunk.

docs.title: Node2D ChunkRendererParent
docs.text: The parent node of all the ChunkRenderer nodes.

docs.title: Dictionary<Vector2I, int> NeighborIndexOffsets
docs.text: A C# Dictionary that maps the Vector2I constants from SandInfo to the amount to add to a cell index to get that specific neighbor.

docs.title: Enum ElementTypes
docs.text:
The possible types an element can be classified as.

Values Description STATIC An unmoving element. SOLID A moving element that can pass through LIQUID and GAS elements. LIQUID A moving element that can pass through GAS elements. GAS A moving element that cannot pass through any element types.

docs.title: Enum ElementFlags
docs.text:
The possible flags an element can have attached to it to give it special interactions and properties.

Values Description FLAMMABLE This element can be set on fire. ACID_RESISTANT This element cannot be destroyed by the ACID default element. INDESTRUCTIBLE This element cannot be destroyed by another element as part of its reaction.

docs.title: WorldStreamer
docs.text:
Inherits: RefCounted < Object

This class is what you will use for saving and loading the simulations created by a PowderSimulation Node.

NOTE: This class defines an override for _Notification(), so if you are extending this class and using those functions, make sure to include super() or the C# equivalent in it so it still calls the parent class functions as well as whatever you put.

docs.title: Public Methods

docs.title: WorldStreamer Open(string WorldPath, PowderSimulation Simulation)
docs.text:
• string WorldPath - The path to the file to open. must point to a file with the .pwdr extension.
  • PowderSimulation Simulation - The simulation node for this WorldStreamer instance to save and load from.

Creates a new WorldStreamer object and assigns it the specified file. WorldPath must point to an existing file with the .pwdr extension.

Returns a new WorldStreamer object if the file is usable; otherwise returns null.

docs.title: WorldStreamer Create(string WorldDirPath, string FileName, PowderSimulation Simulation)
docs.text:
• string WorldDirPath - The path to the folder for this file to be saved in. Usually starts with user://. Must end with /
  • string FileName - The name for the new file to be called. The extension is automatically attached, so no need to add .pwdr to the end of this parameter.
  • PowderSimulation Simulation - The simulation node for this WorldStreamer instance to save and load from.

Creates a new WorldStreamer object and a fresh .pwdr file with the given FileName assigned to it. WorldDirPath must point to a directory in which the file can be created. FileName MUST be different than an already existing file. Otherwise it opens the existing file.

Returns a new WorldStreamer object if the filename and directory path are usable; otherwise returns null.

docs.title: string SaveEmpty(string Name, string Path)
docs.text:
• string Name - The name to be given to the newly created file. The file extension is automatically attached, so no need to add .pwdr to the end of this parameter.
  • string Path - The path to the folder for this file to be saved in. Usually starts with user://. Must end with /

Creates an empty save file. Path must point to a directory in which the new file can be added to. Path also must end with /.

Returns the path to the newly created file.

docs.title: bool IsFileUsable(string Path)
docs.text:
• string Path - The path to the file to check.

Returns whether the given file correctly contains the key and the correct file extension. Basically whether or not the save is initially valid.

docs.title: void Close()
docs.text: Flushes dead chunks, closes the file, and disposes of this object. Note: WorldStreamer will automatically close when it's freed, which happens when it goes out of scope or when it gets assigned with null. In C# the reference must be disposed after we are done using it, this can be done with the using statement or calling the Dispose method directly.

docs.title: bool FlushDeadChunks()
docs.text:
Reads through the file and removes saved chunks that are duplicates. Uses ChunkFileOffsets to determine duplicates. Will most likely fix a corrupted file.

Automatically called when Close is called. Should not be called often, as it rewrites the whole file.

Returns whether or not there were any dead chunks to remove.

docs.title: bool SaveWorld(bool Override)
docs.text:
• bool Override - Whether or not to override the contents of the file, essentially replacing the contents with the current ones.

Saves the world to disk, only operating on the chunks currently active in the simulation.

Returns whether the operation was successful or not.

docs.title: bool LoadWorld()
docs.text:
Replaces the current active chunks in the simulation with the corresponding saved chunks in the file. Does not create chunks.

Returns whether or not there were any currently loaded chunks saved in the file.

docs.title: void SaveChunk(SandInfo.Chunk chunk)
docs.text:
• SandInfo.Chunk chunk - The chunk to save to file.

Saves the given chunk to the file. Creates a dead chunk in the file if there was an old version already saved. The dead chunk can be removed by calling FlushDeadChunks().

docs.title: void UnloadChunk(SandInfo.Chunk chunk)
docs.text:
• SandInfo.Chunk chunk - The chunk to unload.

Saves the given Chunk to the file, and removes it from the simulation. Uses SaveChunk() to save to file, so everything from that description applies here.

docs.title: bool LoadChunk(Vector2I ChunkPosition)
docs.text:
• Vector2I ChunkPosition - The position to load a chunk to.

Replaces or adds a chunk to the simulation with corresponding data from the file.

  • Returns whether the specified chunk position exists in the file.

docs.title: Array[Vector2I] GetAvailableChunks()
docs.text: Returns a Godot Array containing the positions of all chunks saved in the file.

docs.title: The Element Creator Tab
docs.text: In this tutorial, you will learn how to use the Element Creator Tab in the editor to create and edit elements and their basic properties.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: • Menu Overview

docs.title: Menu Overview
docs.text:
This menu contains all the tools needed to edit the basic properties and reactions of elements, as well as add your own. Here are brief descriptions of each button/field and what they do:

Field Name Description Element To Edit The element currently being edited. Select "+ Add Element" to create a new element. Element Name The name of the element. This is the name reflected in the AllElements enum and everywhere else the element is referenced. Element Type Element Types Movement Preset Movement Presets Reactions Reactions Flags Flags Base Color The base color of the element when displayed in game. Noise Strength The strength of the random brightness effect applied to the element's Base Color. Ranges from 0-1, with 1 equal to fully random brightness, and 0 is a flat, unchanging color. Apply Changes This is the button that, when pressed, saves all your changes in the ElementData file included in the plugin and generates the AllElements Enum. Your changes will not be in effect unless you press this button. Delete Current Element Deletes the selected element. You cannot delete default elements. Make sure there are no references of the element in your code before this, since the enum entry will be deleted as well. Reset Defaults Deletes all elements and replaces them with the original set. The original set is all the elements included when you initially download the plugin.

docs.title: Element Types
docs.text:
An element's Type defines which elements can pass through each other when moving. Here is the list of types and what they define:

Type Can Pass Through STATIC Does not move SOLID LIQUID, GAS LIQUID GAS GAS None

docs.title: Movement Presets
docs.text:
An element's Movement Preset defines its behavior and how it moves in the simulation. Here is the list of movement presets and what movement they use:

Movement Preset Movement Description NONE No movement SAND Moves down if nothing is blocking it, otherwise moves diagonally down either left or right LIQUID Same as SAND if nothing is blocking, otherwise moves left or right. Changes directions when hitting another element. STONE Moves down if nothing is blocking it, and only if there are less than two elements directly to the left or right of it. GAS The same as LIQUID, but upside-down. CUSTOM Uses the movement defined in the ElementBehavior assigned to it. See Making Custom ElementBehaviors for more information.

docs.title: Reactions
docs.text:
The reaction editor lets you create simple reactions with other elements without having to use custom ElementBehaviors.

The order of reactions in the Reactions menu is the order they will be executed in. This can sometimes affect the element's intended interaction.

It contains a 3 sections:

  • Marked Neighbors
  • Condition
  • Effect

docs.title: Marked Neighbors
docs.text: The Marked Neighbors are the cells adjacent to the updating cell that get checked against the condition. Click on the buttons around the center cell to mark that corresponding neighbor.

docs.title: Condition
docs.text:
The condition section includes all UI under the (Condition) parentheses, and before the (Effect) parentheses. The reaction loops around all Marked Neighbors and checks them against a condition defined here. The condition has three parts as well: The comparison, the amount, and the element to look for. The comparison can either ==, >=, or <. The element to look for can either be a single element, or Any (any non-AIR element) with exclusions. The comparison basically is you making an if-statement; for example, if the comparison is >=, the amount is 2, and the element is SAND, it would work like this: 

var sand_neighbors: int

if sand_neighbors >= 2:
    do_effect()

Where sand_neighbors is the number of Marked Neighbors that are currently SAND.

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
[Element] refers to the Replace With option under Effect Options.

The effect section has four options for effect types:

Effect Type Description Replace element with [Element] Replaces the currently updating cell with [Element] Replace All Neighbors with [Element] Replaces every adjacent cell with [Element] Replace Marked Neighbors with [Element] Replaces all adjacent cells that are marked in the Marked Neighbors section with [Element] Replace Last Iterated Neighbor with [Element] When running a reaction, all the marked cells get iterated over. This option replaces the cell the iterator stopped on when the condition became true with [Element]. If no MarkedNeighbors are assigned, this will return the updating cell.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Adding flags to an element is a quick way to add unique features to said element.

There are currently two flags available to use on any element:

Flag Name Description INDESTRUCTIBLE Makes the element unchangable by anything other than itself. If a reaction from a different element adjacent to it would change it, it does not get changed. On the other hand, if it gets changed by its own reaction, it still gets changed. FLAMMABLE Allows the element to be set on fire when adjacent to a cell with the FIRE element. It has some configurable properties.

docs.title: FLAMMABLE Properties
docs.text:
These properties appear only when the element has the FLAMMABLE flag.

Propery Name Description Burn Speed How long, in seconds, it takes for the element to burn completely. (if it is already on fire) Spread Resistance The percent chance, from 0.0-1.0, for the element to resist being caught on fire every time a FIRE cell reacts with it. This should be on the higher end if you want visible changes, since it usually attempts to be set on fire very frequently.

docs.title: FireBehavior Explanation
docs.text:
This page will explain how the custom ElementBehavior system (see Making Custom ElementBehaviors) was used to make the behavior for the FIRE element. Here is the code for FireBehavior:

[Tool]
[GlobalClass]
public partial class FireBehavior : ElementBehavior
{

    public override Dictionary<string, byte> _DefaultFields()
    {
        return new Dictionary<string, byte>
        {
            {"R#MovesBeforeExpire", 25},
            {"R#random", 1},
            {"R#direction", 0},
            {"bumps", 0},
        };
    }



    public override void _OnCellUpdate(SandInfo.Cell cell, PowderSimulation sim)
    {

        if(cell.GetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire") <= 0)
        {
            cell.SetElement(Elements.AllElements.AIR);   
        }
        else
        {
            cell.SetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire", (byte)(cell.GetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire") - 1));

            RunGas(cell, sim);
        }

    }


}

docs.title: Let's look at the _DefaultFields function first:
docs.text:
public override Dictionary<string, byte> _DefaultFields()
{
    return new Dictionary<string, byte>
    {
        {"R#MovesBeforeExpire", 25},
        {"R#random", 1},
        {"direction", 0},
        {"bumps", 0},
     };
}

_DefaultFields returns a Dictionary with strings as the keys and bytes as the values.

  • R#MovesBeforeExpire is the number of update ticks passed before it deletes itself, with a starting value of 0-25.

  • R#random is used for the GAS movement that is used in _OnCellUpdate, with a starting value of 0-1.

  • direction is used for the GAS movement preset that is used in _OnCellUpdate, with a starting value of 0.

  • bumps is used for the GAS movement preset that is used in _OnCellUpdate, with a starting value of 0.

Note: when using preset movement within a custom behavior, make sure to include the same fields the preset uses. The fields they use can be found by opening ElementAttributes.cs in the Scripts/CSharp folder of the plugin and looking at MoveTypeDefaultFields.

docs.title: Now let's look at _OnCellUpdate:
docs.text:
public override void _OnCellUpdate(SandInfo.Cell cell, PowderSimulation sim)
{

    if(cell.GetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire") <= 0)
    {
        cell.SetElement(Elements.AllElements.AIR);   
    }
    else
    {
        cell.SetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire", (byte)(cell.GetField("R#MovesBeforeExpire") - 1));

        RunGas(cell, sim);
    }

}

What this code does is replace the cell with AIR if MovesBeforeExpire is zero, and otherwise lower that number by one and run the GAS movement preset. To do this, it uses the cell.GetField and cell.SetField methods to change and access the specific values of that cell's fields.

docs.title: Making Custom ElementBehaviors
docs.text: Making custom ElementBehaviors allows you to make more complicated elements and define their interactions with code.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Setting Up the Custom Behavior
  • Attaching to your Element
  • Function Overrides

See FireBehavior Explanation for an explanation on how this system was used to make the FIRE behavior.

docs.title: Setting Up the Custom Behavior
docs.text:
There are three steps that need to be completed when creating an ElementBehavior-extending script.

  1. Create a new C# script that extends ElementBehavior. Open the newly created script.

  2. Add [Tool] and [GlobalScript] somewhere above the class definition, which allow it to run in-editor and be recognized as a Resource respectively.

  3. Override the base ElementBehavior functions, _OnCellUpdate() and _DefaultFields(). If your IDE's autocomplete adds something like _base.OnCellUpdate(), it is okay to remove it.

Note: You only have to override _DefaultFields() if it is being used.

Note #2: GDScript behaviors are not supported at the moment.

This is what the "Create New Script" menu should contain when making a new ElementBehavior Script.

This is what the base for your ElementBehavior class should look like. If you are not planning on using _DefaultFields(), it is okay to not include it.

docs.title: Attaching to your Element
docs.text:
Once created, for the ElementBehavior to take effect, it needs to be applied to an element. To attach your behavior to an element, you:

  1. Select your desired element.
  2. Change its Movement Preset to CUSTOM.
  3. Open the dropdown menu for the Custom Behavior field and select your behavior.

How to assign a behavior to an element. To apply the FireBehavior in this case, you would select the FireBehavior option from the dropdown.

docs.title: Function Overrides
docs.text:
ElementBehaviors have two functions you can override to add custom interactions with the simulation. These are the functions you can override:

  • void _OnCellUpdate()
  • Dictionary<string, byte> _DefaultFields()

docs.title: void _OnCellUpdate(SandInfo.Cell cell, PowderSimulation sim)
docs.text:
SandInfo.Cell cell - The cell object being updated. PowderSimulation sim - The reference to the PowderSimulation node the cell is a part of.

This should always be overridden in most cases. This function gets called every time the cell updates (once per simulation tick). Use this function to move the element and change its properties using functions like the ones in the Cell Functions page.

Note: when changing values that would affect the visuals of a cell, like changing its element, make sure to mark the cell as updated by using Cell.CellChunk.MarkCellUpdated(Cell).

docs.title: Dictionary<string, byte> _DefaultFields()
docs.text:
This function is used for supplying the default fields for your element. Fields are properties unique to each instance of an element, and each field is limited to an unsigned byte(integer from 0-255) value. Fields carry over when a cell is successfully moved using Cell.TryMove(). To supply your own default fields, make this function return a new Dictionary<string, byte> with the keys being the name it will be accessed with, and the values being the default value for the field. Special Name Cases There are special prefixes you can add to the name of an field to make it initialize different things.

Prefix Effect R# Randomizes the default value every time it is accessed, with the range 0-[initial value], where [initial value] is the value assigned to the key with the R# prefix.

Note: when accessing fields in _OnCellUpdate(), you must include the prefix in the name. Ex. Cell.GetField("R#random")

docs.title: Save Order
docs.text:
This page is mostly for me to reference, since once the save system is done there is little need to know what each binary sequence corresponds to. However, it doesnt hurt to keep this here, does it?

Each .pwdr file is saved in the same way. It represents the simulation as a binary file. Here is the order in which the binary is saved and what each number represents:

When a bullet point is indented, it is instanced a variable number of times within that indentation level.

  • A PascalString that acts as a key and a header: "PWEngine {version number}"

  • A 32-bit integer; the position to put the pointer when reading the file to find the offset dictionary.

  • A 16-bit integer; Number of elements

    • A PascalString for every element's name

  • An 8-bit integer; The number of cell-specific fields each cell is created with

  • A 32-bit integer; the number of chunks saved

    • A 32-bit integer; the X-position of the current chunk

    • A 32-bit integer; the Y-position of the current chunk

    • A 32-bit integer; The number of runs after the cells were compressed (using RLE)

      • A 32-bit integer; The length of the current run (generated with RLE)

      • A 16-bit integer; The element of the current cell, expressed as the index to the name in the lookup table generated above.

        • An 8-bit integer; one of the cell-specific fields the current cell has.

  • A 32-bit integer; The amount of chunks in the file offset dict

    • A 32-bit integer; The X-position of the current chunk in this file offset dictionary

    • A 32-bit integer; The Y-position of the current chunk

    • A 32-bit integer; The file offset of the chunk.
